doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Star student with a secret musical life, then musicology
summary: Expected to excel academically, he led two lives, student and underage kid sneaking out to hear music, until musicology joined them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Do you recall if you had a discussion with your parents about life as a musician or trying to fashion a career in music?

How can I say — I was a star student at an academic high school and before that at the lower levels, and was expected to do something very different than attempting to be a musician, which failed, or becoming a musicologist, which succeeded.

Well you’ve had a long path and your path to being an author, was it influenced by reading the jazz critics that you were referring to, and other authors, and being dissatisfied with what they wrote for the most part?

No I came to it from musicology, not from jazz. Right? I always had sort of two lives — and really from the age of early teens I was leading two lives as the star student and the underage kid who snuck out to hear music. And, “Oh yeah, Mom, I have a friend who has a car.” You know like, no, I’m taking the bus at night to hear stuff in San Francisco you know. And I really led these two lives for six, seven, eight years before I found a way that I could put them together through musicology.
